sources.title: Yousef Saad, Iterative Methods for Sparse Linear Systems, 2nd ed., SIAM, 2003
sources.locator: Complete Chapter 9, §§9.1–9.6, printed pp. 275–296 (PDF pp. 295–316), and complete Chapter 10, §§10.1–10.8, printed pp. 297–368 (PDF pp. 317–388). Directly used passages: §9.3.4, pp. 285–286, left/right GMRES residual minimization; §9.4.1, pp. 287–289, flexible right preconditioning, the saved vectors z_j, and residual minimization over their actual span; §§10.3.1–10.3.2, pp. 301–310, the fixed-pattern recurrence, pivot branch, factor slots, storage, and product fill distinction.

read_evidence.method: Downloaded the complete 567-page PDF to /tmp/prestige-saad-iterative-2e.pdf, extracted all pages with MuPDF to /tmp/prestige-saad-iterative-2e.txt, and read both complete assigned chapter ranges in page-numbered chunks; printed and PDF page headers were checked.

contents.name: Chapter 9 §§9.1–9.3.4: left, right, and split preconditioning; the residual minimized by left and right GMRES
Chapter 9 §9.2: the SPD-preconditioned CG transform and condition-number bound
contents.reason: The corresponding definition, residual map, and CG theorem already live on the published canonical preconditioning page; this pair adds no duplicate theorem.

contents.name: Chapter 9 §9.4.1, pp. 287–288: flexible right preconditioning stores the actual vectors z_j and orthogonalizes A z_j
Chapter 9 §9.4.1, pp. 288–289: the Arnoldi relation gives true residual minimization over x_0 + span{z_1,...,z_m}
Chapter 9 §§9.5–9.6: preconditioned normal equations and the Concus–Golub–Widlund method
contents.reason: Neither normal-equation preconditioning nor the CGW method is in the assigned ILU(0) and residual-metric scope.

contents.name: Chapter 10 §§10.1–10.2: setup/application tradeoffs and Jacobi, SOR, and SSOR preconditioners
contents.reason: The qualitative separation of setup and application is retained, but this pair introduces no stationary preconditioner or convergence result.

contents.name: Chapter 10 §§10.3.1–10.3.2: static-pattern elimination, ILU(0), zero-pivot status, and stored factor pattern
Chapter 10 §§10.3.1–10.3.2: factor storage and the distinction between the L/U slots and product LU
Chapter 10 §10.3.2: an ILU(0) product can have fill outside the original pattern even though factor slots are restricted
Chapter 10 §10.3.2: apply the published ILU(0) recurrence to a fixed tridiagonal pattern
contents.reason: The source supplies the recurrence and pattern convention; all rational factor values for the displayed 3 by 3 instance are computed and verified locally.

contents.name: Chapter 10 §§10.3.3–10.3.5: ILU(p), regular-grid recurrences, and modified ILU
contents.reason: The assigned procedure is fixed-pattern ILU(0); higher fill levels, grid-specific methods, and diagonal compensation are not claimed.

contents.name: Chapter 10 §10.4: threshold ILUT, ILUTP, and Crout variants
contents.reason: Threshold dropping, pivoting, and alternative Crout ordering are outside the fixed-order/fixed-pattern algorithm.

contents.name: Chapter 10 §10.5: approximate inverse preconditioners
contents.reason: No approximate-inverse method or quality theorem is added.

contents.name: Chapter 10 §10.6: symmetric and nonsymmetric reorderings for ILU
contents.reason: The procedure uses a supplied fixed order and proves no ordering heuristic or robustness claim.

contents.name: Chapter 10 §10.7: block preconditioners
contents.reason: The new algorithm is scalar-entry ILU(0), not block ILU.

contents.name: Chapter 10 §10.8: preconditioners for normal equations
contents.reason: No normal-equation method is within the assigned page scope.

sources.title: Richard Barrett et al., Templates for the Solution of Linear Systems: Building Blocks for Iterative Methods, 2nd ed., SIAM, 1994
sources.locator: Complete §3.1.2, Left and right preconditioning, printed pp. 35–36 (PDF pp. 45–46), and complete §3.4.1–3.4.2, Incomplete factorization preconditioners, printed pp. 38–41 (PDF pp. 48–51). The latter includes the two triangular solves, ILU(0) pattern, pivot breakdown, and the explicit distinction between factor slots and the product M=LU.

read_evidence.method: Downloaded the complete 117-page PDF to /tmp/prestige-netlib-templates.pdf, extracted the full text with MuPDF to /tmp/prestige-netlib-templates.txt, and inspected all of §§3.1.2 and 3.4.1–3.4.2 against the printed page headers.

contents.name: §3.1.2: left and right preconditioning alter the residual/variable maps
§3.4.1: incomplete factorization can break down at a zero pivot; applying LU uses forward and backward solves
§3.4.2: ILU(0) keeps factor entries in the selected pattern, while the product matrix can have entries outside it
§3.4.2: the factor/product distinction gives a direct boundary counterexample to a product-pattern inclusion
§3.4.2: point ILU(0) on the input nonzero pattern
contents.reason: The source defines the retained factor pattern; the exact displayed tridiagonal factor values are derived locally.

contents.name: §3.4.2: ILU(p), block incomplete factorizations, and PDE-specific block structure
contents.reason: The assigned algorithm is scalar fixed-pattern ILU(0); no fill-level or block variant is claimed.
